# Tang v00 
_The newest source of barbeque sauce_ 
 
Tang is going to start at a much lower level than Line did. 
Tang is going to be as pure as possible; using compiled Citrus as code instead of the high level Scratch blocks. 
The Initial System Control Set Process or ISCSP will be entirely written in Citrus. 
Tang will be intentionally more Verbose than Line because we intend to rebuild the user friendly "Line" terminal environment on top of Tang. Therefore, names given to any object inside of Tang (An object is any given variable or list in the system) will be used to identify what the object does for the convenience of the programmer. 
 
# Changes 
_What we did_ 
 
1. Implemented the LIMB and VAR systems from Line. 
 
2. Changed the fundamental idea of LIMB to make it run a tad faster, which will make it run a lot faster in the long term. 
 
3. Each process is now given equal priority, in the future, priority can be changed, but for now they all execute side by side, one token at a time. 
 
4. Created a "delete all contents function" for LIMB. 
 
5. Created a dedicated function for deleting a LIMB. 
 
6. Removed the LIMBAct function 
 
7. Created a Citrus component called PUSH that pushes an item to the stack. 
 
8. Processes now delete their stacks when finished running. 
 
9. Processes now delete their dedicated LIMB when finished running. 

10. Every LIMB operation can now be performed in Citrus. LIMB operations that provide outputs will record to the stack of the process that is running them.

11. Due to some specific Citrus processes requiring it, stacks are now required to be made and destroyed manually using the BEGINSTACK and ENDSTACK Citrus components.

12. If the component reader reads a LOOP component, it will reset it's position to the beginning of the process.

13. Processes need assets so they know what state they are in. To create the assets for a process, use the Citrus component [OPENASSETS]. To delete all of the created assets when the process is finished running, use the Citrus component [CLOSEASSETS].

14. Fixed an error in the main Citrus component reading script that caused components to be ignored and the temporary component storage not to be cleared.

15. The temTokenStore LIMB is now actually deleted when a process's assets are destroyed.

16. Expected arguments are now recorded in the database. If you put MAKE after anything but exactly "LIMB", it won't do anything because LIMB is the parent of the MAKE argument.

17. Arguments are now stored with their parent's names appended to the front like LIMB.ADD or LIMB.MAKE in the registry database.

18. Limb operations are now case sensitive.

19. Prevented processes that don't have loops from looping indefinitely.
 
# Notes 
_What we have to say_ 
 
The format of the Citrus language in Tang is much different than the Lime system in Line. For now, instead of being split by a specified token, each argument is surrounded by hard brackets with no spaces in-between. [Just][Like][This] [VAR $index + 5] Syntax is also TBD, so take that with a grain of salt. Additionally, we hope to have a compiler that can turn Lime into Citrus.  
The fun thing about working at a level this low is that you don't need to think about how the user might want to customize, because realistically why would you want to rename anything here when you won't even know it exists?

Hey guys its me the real Andrew Tanenbaum im here to say that this project is hot garbage 
It's so cool to see the lists flicker to life when I turn everything on. 
Even now this project is so complicated that I am a little bit intimidated by the thought of documenting it... 
Each LIMB function has two areas: preparing the variables of the function for the specific state of the LIMB, and the actual execution of the function. For every LIMB function, the data requirements are different, so I can't just use the same one for everything or else I gain a ton of redundant data.  
The processes LIMB stores the names of the LIMBs that are currently being ran. The processesInstructionPointers LIMB stores at what step each of those processes are at. The key selling point about this system is that I don't have to think too hard about it. It just kinda makes sense.
